origin.description: Convert an annual, quarterly, or monthly ts to dates at the first of the month.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A ts whose frequency is 1, 4, or 12.

arguments.name: offset
arguments.text: Added to time(x) before the year is taken. It does not move the cycle.

origin.details: time(x) is the numeric time, then offset is added. Frequency 1 pastes year-1-1. Frequency 4 pastes the year of floor(time + 0.001) and month 3 * (cycle - 1) + 1. Frequency 12 uses that year and the cycle as the month. Any other frequency stops with "unable to convert ts time to Date class". A fractional annual time is not an unambiguous date.
origin.example:
x <- ts(1:3, start = c(2000, 2), frequency = 12)
cat(paste(as.character(as.Date.ts(x)), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Convert an annual, quarterly, or monthly ts to dates at the first of the month.

arguments.name: offset
arguments.text: Added to the numeric time. The cycle is computed from the original start.

translation.details: The year is floor(time + offset + 0.001). Quarterly months are 1, 4, 7, and 10 from the cycle. Monthly months are the cycle. The strings are parsed as year-month-1. A negative year string is rejected, as base as.Date rejects it.
translation.example:
from zoo.as_date import as_date_ts, format_dates
from zoo.as_zoo import Ts
import numpy as np
x = Ts(np.arange(1, 4), start=(2000, 2), frequency=12)
print(" ".join(format_dates(as_date_ts(x))))
